analog: Cuban Missile Crisis, October 1962 (with message-latency data)
t0: 1962-10-16 (US President briefed on missile photos; ExComm convened)

sources.title: Office of the Historian, US Dept of State: The Cuban Missile Crisis, October 1962

HISTORY: Hotline established between Washington and Moscow (Aug 30, 1963): messages could take six hours; nearly 12 hours to receive and decode Khrushchev's ~3,000-word settlement message

points.event: Oct 16: briefing; forces at normal readiness
Oct 22: public address, quarantine announced; US forces to DEFCON 3
Oct 24: quarantine in effect; Strategic Air Command to DEFCON 2 (highest US level ever reached)
Oct 27 'Black Saturday': U-2 shot down over Cuba; closest point

threat.notes: extent = US alert level on a stated ordinal map: DEFCON 5 = 0, 4 = 0.25, 3 = 0.5, 2 = 0.75, 1 = 1 (never reached). It is escalation, not spread through a population. The DEFCON dates and U-2 shoot-down are standard record (s3) but were not seen verbatim in a snippet this pass. De-escalation after Oct 28 (event list) is not given a number because the date SAC left DEFCON 2 was not confirmed.

events.event: Oct 28: Soviet leader publicly announces the sites will be dismantled

message_latency_hours.notes: official messages could take ~6 h; the ~3,000-word settlement letter took nearly 12 h to receive and decode; both sides also used TV/radio broadcasts because they were faster

fragments.had: obsolete Jupiter missiles in Turkey that could be traded away
first settlement offer: withdraw missiles for a no-invasion pledge (letter of Oct 26)
second, public offer adding the Turkey missiles (Oct 27)

fragments.who: a back channel (the Attorney General and the Soviet ambassador)

fragments.notes: agreement signed June 20, 1963; operational Aug 30, 1963 (t=318, s4)

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented dates (days after Oct 16 1962), not a measured distribution: p10 = first settlement letter Oct 26 (t=10), median = public resolution Oct 28 (t=12), p90 = hotline agreement June 20 1963 (t=247), the structural fix for the communication gap. Within the 12 days each message still took ~6-12 h in transit and decoding (s4).

deploy.notes: Oct 28 announcement to formal end of the naval quarantine on Nov 20, 1962 (23 days).

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative and deliberately modest. The part AI plausibly speeds up is transport and translation: the settlement letter took ~12 h to receive and decode (s4); machine translation and summarization of a 3,000-word letter is a minutes-scale task, far inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry). The decisions themselves were human deliberation and should stay human. Assumed: the same exchanges with ~12 h less latency per round, so the deal assembles ~1 day sooner (day 11 instead of 12). This film must not imply AI should be near nuclear decisions; AI here only carries and clarifies messages between people.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: Alert levels jumped two steps in 8 days while each message between the two leaders took 6-12 hours to cross and decode; the fix for that latency (a direct link) took 247 days to agree.
